sections.h2: Who do I call in Galena about my tax bill?
sections.html:
Two county offices share the work. The Assessor builds the list of taxable property, and the Collector of Revenue bills and gathers the money. Both are in Galena.

  • Collector of Revenue: 108 E. 4th Street, P.O. Box 256, Galena, MO 65656; 417-357-6124; the courthouse is open weekdays from eight to four and closes for state and federal holidays.
  • Assessor: 106 E. 5th Street, P.O. Box 135, Galena, MO 65656; real estate line (417) 357-6145; personal property line (417) 357-6141; same weekday hours.

The Assessor's page lays out the calendar. Assessment books normally close around July 1 and go to the County Clerk, who sends the figures on to each taxing district. The districts then set their rates, typically by September 1. The Assessor has no say in those rates.

The Assessor's office also keeps the tax maps, adjusting property lines whenever the Recorder of Deeds forwards a warranty deed, per the Assessor's description of its mapping duties. On the Collector's side, the staff directory names separate deputies for real estate, personal property, merchant licensing and the SB190 tax freeze, so ask for the real estate desk when you call about a house, and keep the parcel number handy.

sections.h2: What is the due date for the 2026 bill?
sections.html:
The Collector's announcement says statements for 2026 went into the mail on Friday, November 13, and online payment has been open since November 6. Payment is due by December 31, and a bill still open on January 1 is delinquent.

Anything sent by post must carry a U.S. Post Office postmark dated December 31 or earlier. The Collector's home page adds several practical notes:

  • Card numbers are no longer taken verbally over the phone. Pay at the office or call the number printed on your statement.
  • Debit and credit card payments carry a fee of 2.4%, with a $1.95 floor.
  • A drop box at the north entrance of the Historic Courthouse is emptied daily.
  • A paid receipt can be printed, or shown on a phone, at the license bureau.

Read your statement for errors, including the mailing address. To change an address, call 417-357-6124.

sections.h2: Is the senior tax freeze open right now?
sections.html:
No. The Collector's home page says the application process for the Senior Citizen Property Tax Credit Freeze is closed. The staff list includes a lead for the SB190 tax freeze, who is the person to ask about the next window.

A second benefit comes from the state: the Missouri Property Tax Credit Claim, filed with the Department of Revenue, refunds part of the tax or rent paid for some seniors, disabled owners and renters. Phone the Collector's office at 417-357-6124 to find out whether you fit either program before the next filing season.

sections.h2: How do I argue against my assessed value?
sections.html:
Phone the Assessor on (417) 357-6145 and ask this year's Board of Equalization deadline. RSMo 138.060 tells the county board to decide valuation appeals in a summary way and adds that no presumption favors the assessor. Where a parcel's assessed value jumped by 15% or more over the previous assessment, other than through new construction or improvement, the assessor must show the figure is not above market value.

If you still owe the bill while arguing, RSMo 139.031 permits payment under protest. The full bill is paid before delinquency, a written statement of your reasons goes to the collector, and a circuit court action starts within 90 days. A taxpayer with a timely State Tax Commission appeal on file for that year skips the separate court action.

sections.h2: What if the bill goes past January 1?
sections.html:
Penalties and interest start running. RSMo 140.150 allows delinquent land to go to sale each August, on the fourth Monday. The collector writes to the owner of record before publication, and the owner may clear the tax, penalty, interest and costs any time ahead of the sale.

A seller who carries an open bill should plan to pay it from closing proceeds. Get the exact payoff from the Collector, since penalties change with the date, and pass that number to the title company. The Collector takes payment at its Galena office and in the courthouse drop box.

sections.h2: Is Stone County growing, and what do homes cost?
sections.html:
Population is rising. The Census Bureau's April 2020 base was 31,079 and the July 2025 estimate is 32,503, a gain of 4.6%. Over the same stretch St. Louis County and Stoddard County each lost 1.4%. Stone County belonged to the Branson micropolitan area until 2023, and the Branson West Municipal Airport sits two nautical miles west of the city of Branson West.

Density is 67.0 people per square mile on 463.83 square miles of land. Typical rent is $896, and owners report monthly costs of $1,451 with a mortgage and $476 without. About 88.1% of residents lived at the same address a year earlier. Among adults 25 and older, 91.8% finished high school and 24.8% finished a four-year degree or went further.

The Census lists 21,225 housing units for July 2025 and 13,530 households for 2020 to 2024, so the housing stock sits well above the count of households. When you set a price, compare your parcel with sales of similar houses in your own community and school district rather than leaning on the county's $249,000 figure.

sections.h2: What sort of place is Stone County?
sections.html:
It lies in southwest Missouri along the Arkansas line, bordered by Christian, Taney, Barry and Lawrence counties and by Carroll County, Arkansas. Galena is the seat and Kimberling City the largest city. Branson West, Reeds Spring, Crane, Hurley and Blue Eye round out the list of cities and villages, and part of the Mark Twain National Forest lies inside the county. Water covers 47 of its 511 square miles, or 9.2%.

The county counted 9,921 residents in 1970 and 31,076 in 2020. It was organized on February 10, 1851, and takes its name from William Stone, an early Maryland settler. The Census table adds the housing details.

Reeds Spring operates the most schools of those districts, with primary, elementary, intermediate, middle and high schools, and the Gibson Technical Center there offers vocational classes for grades 9 to 12. Libraries operate in Blue Eye, Crane, Galena and Kimberling City. Employment reached 5,681 in 2023, up 8.2% on 2022, and retail sales totaled $359,943,000 in 2022.

faqs.q: Where can I find the Stone County Collector?
faqs.a: At 108 E. 4th Street in Galena, or by mail at P.O. Box 256, Galena, MO 65656. Call 417-357-6124. Courthouse hours run weekdays, eight to four.

faqs.q: Do they take credit cards for property tax?
faqs.a: Yes, in person, online, or through the number on your statement. The Collector lists a 2.4% fee with a $1.95 minimum, and no card numbers are given verbally by phone.

faqs.q: On what day does a Stone County bill become delinquent?
faqs.a: January 1. The bill is due by December 31, and mail needs a U.S. Post Office postmark of that date or earlier.

faqs.q: Which body decides the tax rate?
faqs.a: The taxing districts set it, usually by September 1. The county Assessor values property but has no part in rate setting, according to the county's own page.

faqs.q: Can I apply for the senior freeze today?
faqs.a: Not at the moment. The Collector's home page lists that application process as closed, so call 417-357-6124 to learn when it will reopen.
